title: An existing COD customer keeps its old limit on release day
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: On production, a COD customer had a $1,000 credit limit before the release.
  • You are signed in to production (the live app, app.shopview.com) as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Trucks Hill 2 on the production test account.
  • On production, customer {Customer-A} held COD with a credit limit of $1,000.00 before the release reached production (written down then, with a screenshot).
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S11-07 Cash.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the credit limit still reads $1,000.00 (the release did not change it).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11680 (Story 11, Release day: what changes for existing users)

  • S11-R11: “An existing COD or Credit Hold customer with a credit limit above $0 keeps that limit on release day.”
  • Key Decisions: “The rule applies only to customers created or edited after release: an existing COD or Credit Hold customer with a limit stored from before keeps it until the customer is next edited in Edit Customer, updated by the contacts import, or updated through the Public API with a credit term or credit limit or moved to COD or Credit Hold by Move Customers; each of those saves $0.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf): canvas pages "1 List and row menus", "5 New Customer", "8 Over Credit warning" (the pages the PRD names for this story). The design (read in full on 23 Oct 2026) does not draw this case's screen or state, so no design picture is attached; the expected results above come from the PRD.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - needs the before values taken on production shortly before the release reaches production; run on production after the release
